primitives.name: Physiological Load Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: 1 David Pizarro, Alba Pr ́axedes, Bruno Travassos, Bruno Gon ̧calves and Alberto Moreno How the Number of Players and Floaters' Positioning Changes the Offensive Performance during Futsal Small-Sided and Conditioned Games Reprinted from: Int.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'L': 'dimensionless load index', 't': 'time in seconds', 'P': 'power output in watts', 'M': 'mass in kilograms'}
primitives.assumptions: Load is proportional to power-to-mass ratio and duration of exertion; assumes constant environmental conditions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Load exceeds 1.2L leads to fatigue-induced performance degradation.

layer2.mapping: Maps training intensity to cumulative fatigue using time-weighted power outputs across repeated sprints.
layer2.telemetry: Heart rate variability, lactate threshold, and sprint velocity decline.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When D < 0.5, error propagation increases beyond acceptable variance.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphism between external focus strategies and stochastic control theory in reinforcement learning.
layer2.telemetry: Execution accuracy, movement variability, and retention test scores.

primitives.name: Recovery Biomarker Integration
primitives.verbatim_quote: 23 Ching-Feng Cheng, Yu-Hsuan Kuo, Wei-Chieh Hsu, Chu Chen and Chi-Hsueh Pan Local and Remote Ischemic Preconditioning Improves Sprint Interval Exercise Performance in Team Sport Athletes Reprinted from: Int.
primitives.assumptions: Biomarker levels decay exponentially; recovery score is linear combination of cortisol, creatine kinase, and IL-6.
primitives.breakdown_regime: R < 0.3 indicates suboptimal recovery and increased injury risk.

layer2.mapping: Kernel density estimation of biomarker trajectories to predict readiness for next session.
layer2.telemetry: Cortisol, CK, IL-6, and subjective fatigue ratings.

The three core primitives—physiological load index, skill acquisition via differential learning, and recovery biomarker integration—are unified under a Bayesian hierarchical model where each component contributes to a latent performance variable. Physiological load index acts as a driver of fatigue, while differential learning modulates adaptation efficiency. Recovery biomarkers provide feedback to adjust future load parameters. These components interact through a recursive update mechanism that adjusts training intensity based on observed performance and recovery outcomes. Failure modes include overtraining when L > 1.2, poor motor learning when D < 0.5, and delayed recovery when R < 0.3. Dualities emerge in how external focus (learning) and internal load (physiology) co-regulate performance. The system exhibits non-linear dynamics due to feedback loops and temporal dependencies.
